comments.author: @MrLaureus
comments.text: You portray Madeira as though it were some idyllic community of innocent Hobbits, conveniently untouched by the darker realities of Atlantic history. As a Madeiran, I find it particularly striking that you omit the island’s involvement in, and material benefit from, slavery and the trafficking and exploitation of North Africans, Guanches, and sub-Saharan Africans. Madeira was not merely an innocent spectator to these processes; it was part of the economic and human networks that sustained them. The terraces, levadas, churches, and manor houses that now make up its celebrated cultural landscape did not, after all, materialise by divine grace. To romanticise that landscape while overlooking the coerced labour, exploitation, and suffering that contributed to producing it is not simply an omission: it is a sanitised version of history.
